events.text: It was nearly two in the morning. The old city hospital was unusually quiet.
Most of the staff had gone home, leaving behind the soft humming of machines, flickering fluorescent lights, and the distant sound of rain hitting the windows.
Dr. John K. Smith had been working for almost twelve hours. Exhausted, he sat at his desk, finishing his coffee and preparing to leave.
Just as he picked up his coat, the phone rang.
Doctor Smith? We need you on the twelfth floor. A patient's condition is suddenly getting worse.
All right, I'm coming.
The time was 2:13 AM.
He grabbed his stethoscope, stepped into the hallway, and headed toward the elevator.
The hospital had twelve floors. At least, that's what everyone believed.
John entered the elevator and pressed the button for the twelfth floor.
The doors closed. The elevator began moving.
Three… four… five… six…
Everything seemed normal.
Then the lights flickered. The elevator jerked violently, and John grabbed the handrail.
The display continued changing. Eight… nine… ten… eleven… twelve… But the elevator didn't stop.
John looked at the floor indicator. The number changed. … The elevator became colder.
That's impossible.
A faint sound of a child laughing echoed from somewhere inside.
Doctor...
John turned around. Nobody was there.
The elevator doors slowly opened. And beyond them was a corridor he had never seen before.
A long, dark corridor stretched in front of him.
The walls were covered in peeling paint. Dust lay across the floor. Old wheelchairs stood against the walls, and rusty hospital beds sat outside rooms with half-open doors.
The lights flickered one after another, illuminating the corridor in brief flashes.
John stepped out of the elevator. A sign above the hallway read: Floor 13 — Emergency Ward.
This hospital doesn't have a thirteenth floor.
He turned back toward the elevator. The doors closed. John rushed forward and pressed the button.
Nothing happened. He pressed it again. Nothing.
The elevator was gone. Where it had been, there was now nothing but a solid wall.
John stepped backward, breathing faster. From somewhere down the corridor, a woman's voice called out.
Doctor... (distant woman's call, Floor 13)
John raised his flashlight and slowly walked toward the sound.
He entered an old ward. There were ten beds. Every bed was occupied.
The patients were lying perfectly still, facing the walls.
John approached the first bed.
Hello?
Can you hear me?
The patient slowly turned his head. His face was pale. His eyes were sunken, and his lips were almost colorless.
You are late, Doctor.
How do you know who I am?
John K. Smith.
We have been waiting for you.
John moved toward the next bed. An elderly woman began laughing softly.
Another patient whispered from the corner.
(whisper) ...you forgot us.
Then, one by one, all the patients turned toward him. Their heads moved at exactly the same time.
They spoke together.
You don't remember... but we remember you.
John ran out of the ward.
But as he reached the corridor, he heard a little girl's voice.
Doctor Uncle... don't leave.
He turned. A little girl was sitting on a hospital bed, holding an old cloth doll.
She was staring directly at him.
Why are you here?
Because tonight... it's your turn.
John hurried down the hallway until he found a door marked Medical Records.
He pushed it open. Inside were hundreds of old files, dusty cabinets, broken chairs, and papers scattered across the floor.
He turned on his phone's flashlight and started searching for a way out.
Then he noticed a file lying open on a desk. The name on it made his blood run cold.
John K. Smith. His photograph was attached to the front. His date of birth. His home address. Even his current hospital ID number.
John opened the file with trembling hands. The first page contained a disturbing report.
He flipped to the next page. The next page was dated eighteen years ago.
This can't be happening... (script: This can't be real)
At the bottom of the file, a final line was written in red ink: Status — never discharged.
A voice behind him said,
Now you remember, Doctor?
John slowly turned.
An old man stood in the doorway, wearing a faded white doctor's coat.
The old doctor had sunken eyes and a face covered in deep wrinkles. He looked as though he hadn't slept in decades.
What is this place?
Why is my name in that file?
This floor belongs to those who never left.
I'm alive! I was working downstairs!
I need to get out of here!
Everyone says the same thing.
Where is the elevator?
Find it.
If it allows you to return, you may leave.
And if it doesn't?
Then you'll be waiting for the next doctor.
Suddenly, every light in the corridor went out.
A red EXIT sign glowed in the darkness. And from somewhere far away, a bell rang.
John ran. He didn't know where he was going. He only knew he had to escape.
He opened one door — another hospital corridor.
He opened another. The same corridor. The same wheelchairs. The same flickering lights. He ran faster.
Then he saw the little girl standing in the middle of the hallway. She was holding her doll.
Doctor... why are you running?
But when he passed her, he noticed something. The doll's face looked exactly like his.
No...
Behind John, every patient began appearing in the corridor. One by one. Standing silently. Watching him.
John sprinted toward the end of the hallway.
And there it was. An elevator. Its doors were already open.
He jumped inside. The display flashed. The elevator suddenly began descending.
Dr. John K. Smith... your shift is not over yet.
No! Open! Please!
Thirteen… twelve… eleven… ten…
Finally, the elevator stopped. The doors opened.
Morning sunlight filled the lobby.
John stumbled out onto the floor, gasping for breath.
It was six in the morning.
The hospital lobby was busy again. Nurses were moving between desks, patients were waiting, and sunlight streamed through the windows.
A nurse saw John and rushed toward him.
Dr. Smith! Where have you been? We've been looking for you all night!
I was on the thirteenth floor.
What thirteenth floor?
The elevator took me there.
There were patients... an old doctor... a little girl...
Doctor... this hospital has never had a thirteenth floor.
I saw it. I was there.
Maybe you need some rest, Doctor.
Maybe... maybe I just need some rest.
John walked away, trying to convince himself it had all been a nightmare.
But as he passed the reception desk, an old register lying open began turning pages by itself. It stopped on a blank page. A name slowly appeared.
Dr. John K. Smith. Floor 13. Shift: tonight — 2:13 AM.
That same night, the hospital CCTV cameras recorded an empty reception.
At exactly 2:13 AM, the elevator doors opened by themselves. Nobody was inside.
The floor indicator began changing. Twelve… then…
Dr. John K. Smith... please report to Floor 13.
A few seconds later, the reception phone rang.
Is there any doctor available?
We have a new patient on the thirteenth floor.
What thirteenth floor? (stands in for: What? There's no thirteenth floor.)
His name is John K. Smith.
The phone went dead.
The elevator doors slowly closed. The display remained glowing red.
And somewhere behind those doors… a man in a white coat was waiting.
The end.
